Device header defines PLAY1 as the non-secure PLAY instance outside the secure build.
SDK describes PLAY as lookup tables programmed to any logical function, cascadable into more complex functions.

SDK usage text: configure input multiplexers, then lookup tables, then output multiplexers; HAL_PLAY_Start locks the configuration and makes the kernel clock operational; only after it may PLAY outputs be connected to GPIOs. It also gives the truth table encoding.
SDK documents the truth table: combination ID = IN0 + 2*IN1 + 4*IN2 + 8*IN3 and the value is the sum of O(y) * 2^y; AND of IN1 and IN0 is 0x8888.
SDK: to update lookup table configurations call HAL_PLAY_Stop first; it disables interrupts, clears flags and unlocks the configuration; outputs should be disconnected meanwhile to avoid glitches.
SDK: by default HAL_PLAY_Init does not enable the PLAY clock (USE_HAL_PLAY_CLK_ENABLE_MODEL is HAL_CLK_ENABLE_NO).
SDK: a software trigger or edge trigger write takes 3 cycles of the PLAY kernel clock plus 2 PCLK cycles; the SDK bounds it by 4000 ms.
SDK defines the edge trigger write HAL_PLAY_Start ends with: HAL_BUSY when a write is pending, then it waits on the write-busy flag up to the given limit of HAL ticks.
SDK: the input multiplexer minimum pulse width is a value from 0x00 to 0xFF.
SDK code generator turns an expression of A, B, C, D into a truth table by setting bit i when the expression holds with A = bit 0, B = bit 1, C = bit 2, D = bit 3 of i.
SDK: the PLAY kernel clock is LSE by default and can be LSI, PLL2P, HSE, HSI or HSI48.
ST gate_xor example for NUCLEO-G564RE enables the PLAY1 clock, initializes PLAY1 and selects LSI as its kernel clock.
ST gate_xor example configures input multiplexer 4 on external input IN4 with edge detection bypassed and a minimum pulse width of 100.
ST gate_xor example writes 0x6666 for A ^ B with A on lookup table input 0, B on input 1 and the default source on inputs 2 and 3 that the table ignores.
ST gate_xor example sets PC13 (the user button input PLAY1_IN4) to alternate function 14, push-pull, pull-down, high speed.
ST gate_xor example sets PD11 (PLAY1_OUT0) to alternate function 14, push-pull, no pull, high speed.
ST gate_xor example enables LSI (32 kHz) and sets the PLAY1 kernel clock divider to 1.
ST gate_xor README: a filtered input is taken into account only if stable for a number of PLAY clock cycles set by the filter configuration.
ST gate_xor example lists the STM32 HAL GPIO and PLAY and STM32 LL GPIO and PLAY components among its CMSIS components.
ST signal_routing example writes 0xAAAA for the expression A.
ST signal_routing example selects LSI as PLAY1 kernel clock.
ST counter_3bits example writes 0x5555 for the expression !A.

PA8/CC1 and PA9/CC2 have separate DBCC-controlled 5.1 kOhm pull-downs after reset. The PWR dead-battery disable control overrides both.
PWR_UCPDR.UCPD_DBDIS resets clear. Setting bit 0 disables USB Type-C dead-battery behavior on both CC1 and CC2.
HAL disables USB-C dead-battery behavior through LL_PWR_DisableUCPDDeadBattery.
The low-level disable function sets PWR_UCPDR_UCPD_DBDIS in PWR->UCPDR.

assumptions: Acceptance binds authoring bytes, not complete silicon knowledge or runtime behavior.

PLAY units cover combinational functions of pads and software triggers through one lookup table each; registered outputs, clock gates, edge detection, edge triggers, interrupts, EXTI, low-power modes and security attributes are not covered.
No PLAY timing, propagation delay, glitch behavior, filter accuracy or LSI frequency is claimed; register read-back through SDK getters is not a measurement.
A PLAY unit's initialization stops and restarts PLAY1, holding the kernel-clock features of every other unit in reset meanwhile; all units initialize before main's loop.

PA8/PA9 GPIO or PLAY allocation requires explicit project permission ucpd_dead_battery=disable_permitted_on_both_cc_pins. Either allocation selects one startup write disabling dead-battery on both pins. Incompatible with retaining USB-C dead-battery support.

capabilities.description: Two-input logic gate in the PLAY: two input pads, each through its own PLAY1 input multiplexer and filter, combined by one lookup table into and, or, xor, nand, nor or xnor, driven on an output pad through an output multiplexer. Generated component: init only, configured once at start-up. Pads and multiplexers are those the pinout descriptor routes to PLAY1 and the target board permits; PLAY1 is shared with the other PLAY units.

One input pad routed through a PLAY1 input multiplexer and filter and one lookup table, unchanged or inverted, to an output pad through an output multiplexer. Generated component: init only, configured once at start-up. Pads and multiplexers are those the pinout descriptor routes to PLAY1 and the target board permits; PLAY1 is shared with the other PLAY units.

One input pad combined in the PLAY with a software trigger the application writes: the pad through a PLAY1 input multiplexer and filter is input A, the trigger is input B, one lookup table computes and, or, xor, nand, nor or xnor, driven on an output pad through an output multiplexer. Generated component with init, set trigger and get trigger. PLAY1 is shared with the other PLAY units.
CRC-32 (ISO 3309, zlib) of a buffer of bytes on the hardware CRC unit: a generated unit with init and a one-call computation. The whole CRC unit belongs to it.

Independent watchdog with a chosen reset time: a generated unit that prepares the watchdog, and start, refresh, the time actually set and a state for the application. Once started it resets the microcontroller unless refreshed in time and cannot be stopped; a start that fails may leave it running.

implementations.guidance: Shared integration of every generated PLAY unit: switches on the SDK's PLAY and GPIO modules in the captured HAL configuration and adds the STM32 HAL and LL GPIO and PLAY components that the STM32CubeG5 PLAY examples list to the foundation's CMSIS component list, so the SDK's CMake builds stm32g5xx_hal_play.c and stm32g5xx_hal_gpio.c. No PLAY, clock or pad setup of its own; the units do that.

implementations.guidance: Generated component owns two PLAY1 input multiplexers, one lookup table, one output multiplexer and three pads. the unit_init, called from main after mx_system_init, sets both input pads to alternate function 14 with the chosen pulls, globally resets and initializes PLAY1 with LSI as kernel clock on the first PLAY unit (stopping it on a later one), writes the two input multiplexers (external input, edge detection bypassed, the chosen minimum pulse width), the truth table of the chosen function with A on lookup table input 0 and B on input 1, the output multiplexer on the table's direct output, starts PLAY1 with no edge trigger, checks the selected PLAY mux, LUT and filter fields through SDK getters and only then connects the output pad. Unused table inputs 2 and 3 keep the SDK default source; every listed table ignores them. Do not configure PLAY1, its clock or these pads elsewhere; every other PLAY user must be a generated PLAY unit. No timing, glitch or electrical behavior is established.

interface.setup: Initialized from main after mx_system_init by {{unit}}_init(); a failure makes main return -1. Header bkpt_components/{{unit}}.h. No manual PLAY1, PLAY clock, LSI or pad setup.
interface.pads: In: {{pad_a_name}} (A, PLAY1 {{a_name}}, pull {{pull_a}}) and {{pad_b_name}} (B, PLAY1 {{b_name}}, pull {{pull_b}}). Out: {{pad_out_name}} through PLAY1 {{out_name}} from {{lut_name}}'s direct output. Alternate function 14, high speed, push-pull; the output pad is connected only after PLAY1 starts.
interface.function: {{function}} by truth table {{truth_table}}, A on lookup table input 0, B on input 1. Unused table inputs keep the SDK default source; the table ignores them.
interface.filter: Each pad input passes a PLAY1 input filter with a minimum pulse width of {{min_pulse_width}} cycles of the PLAY1 kernel clock, LSI with divider 1, edge detection bypassed. No timing is claimed.
interface.scope: PLAY1 is shared by generated PLAY units only: nothing else may configure PLAY1, its kernel clock or these pads. Each unit's init stops and restarts PLAY1. No registered outputs, clock gates, edge triggers, interrupts, low-power or security attributes; no timing, glitch or electrical behavior established.

implementations.guidance: Generated component owns one PLAY1 input multiplexer, one lookup table, one output multiplexer and two pads. the unit_init, called from main after mx_system_init, sets the input pad to alternate function 14 with the chosen pull, globally resets and initializes PLAY1 with LSI as kernel clock on the first PLAY unit (stopping it on a later one), writes the input multiplexer (external input, edge detection bypassed, the chosen minimum pulse width), the truth table of buffer or invert with the input on lookup table input 0, the output multiplexer on the table's direct output, starts PLAY1 with no edge trigger, checks the selected PLAY mux, LUT and filter fields through SDK getters and only then connects the output pad. Unused table inputs 1 to 3 keep the SDK default source; both tables ignore them. Do not configure PLAY1, its clock or these pads elsewhere; every other PLAY user must be a generated PLAY unit. implementations.guidance: Generated component owns the watchdog handle. Generated init only prepares it: the application calls start when it is ready, and from then on must call refresh within the reset time or the microcontroller resets. The watchdog cannot be stopped or reconfigured before a reset, so start it only when the refresh path is in place. The reset time is the selected number of milliseconds at the nominal 32kHz of the low-speed internal oscillator; timeout_ms reports the time the driver set, and the oscillator's real frequency shifts it. While start runs, state reports 3 and refresh returns HAL_BUSY and writes nothing: a refresh writes the reload key, the reference manual states that any key but the access key write-protects the watchdog's registers again, and the SDK writes the access key and then the prescaler and the reload value, so a refresh from an interrupt inside start could leave the watchdog with other values than the unit reports. The SDK enables the watchdog before it waits for its registers, and those waits can fail: when start returns an error other than busy, state reports 2, the watchdog may be running with a reset time that is not known, timeout_ms reports 0xFFFFFFFF, refresh still restarts the count, start cannot be tried again, and a reset may follow. No window (a refresh is allowed at any time) and no early interrupt. refresh may be called from the owning thread or an interrupt, and is refused from an interrupt that arrives while start runs; start from the thread only. Behaviour while a debugger halts the core and in low-power modes, and the option bytes, are not covered. Build does not exercise the reset.

While it runs, state is 3 and refresh is refused. Any other result is a failed start after which the watchdog may be running with a reset time that is not known: state is 2 and a reset may follow. Thread only.
interface.refresh: {{unit}}_refresh(): checked HAL_OK restarts the count; call it more often than the reset time. Thread or interrupt. HAL_ERROR before any start; HAL_BUSY, with nothing written, while start is running; after a failed start the count is restarted all the same.
interface.timeout: {{unit}}_timeout_ms(): the reset time the driver set, in milliseconds of the nominal oscillator; 0 before start; 0xFFFFFFFF while start runs and after a failed start, when it is not known.
interface.scope: No window, no early interrupt, nominal 32kHz oscillator. The reset time is not measured, the reset is not exercised by a build, and a failed start is not recoverable.
interface.state: {{unit}}_state(): 0 not started, 1 running with the reported time, 2 a start failed and the watchdog may be running, 3 start is running (seen only from an interrupt).
